ideas.title: Core: argument checks name the parameter
ideas.text: Eight core guards throw `new ArgumentException("habitId")` (also "directory", "plant"): the parameter name becomes the message and ParamName stays null (CA2208; Ledger.cs:149, :162, :182, :220, :252, SaveStore.cs:68, SundialState.cs:62, Companions.cs:46). Throw `new ArgumentException("<what is wrong>", nameof(habitId))`, keeping the exception type. No signature changes, so it qualifies under 0012 (c) with a dotnet test that pins ParamName.

ideas.title: Sundial: SundialService argument checks name the parameter
ideas.text: The same CA2208 shape in the in-place app file SundialService.cs:124 (directory), :333 and :452 (habitId). Same fix as the core idea; the file is one of the six that 0012 (c) lets change on dotnet test alone, with a test that pins ParamName and the Unity-only callers listed.

ideas.title: Core: GardenDay gets <= and >= beside < and >
ideas.text: GardenDay implements IComparable<GardenDay> and defines ==, !=, < and > (GardenDay.cs:55-58) but not <= and >= (CA1036), so a caller writes `a.Index <= b.Index` or `!(a > b)`. Add the two operators; purely additive (step A, 0004), with a dotnet test.

ideas.title: Core: LedgerJson reads and writes the whole Habits and Tends arrays
ideas.text: After b7ed44f the row codec has one owner, but the loops around it are still typed twice: SundialSave.cs:69-87 and TerrariumSave.cs:83-98 read the Habits and Tends arrays row by row, and SundialSave.cs:101-116 against TerrariumSave.cs:121-136 write them (jscpd, 118 to 201 tokens each). A LedgerJson.ReadHabits/ReadTends/WriteHabits/WriteTends pair (step A) lets both saves drop the loops; the SundialSave half then lands under 0012 (c) with the golden row tests (f11db8f). It continues findings #12 and #14.

ideas.title: Assets: two 16-bit pngs, an owner call on requantising
ideas.text: Two tracked pngs under apps/*/Assets are 16 bits per sample (node tools/assets/census.mjs --rev 8670dd1 --out <temp dir>, class png-16-bit): apps/terrarium/Assets/Art/Textures/moss-repaint.png (2053436 bytes estimated to save) and apps/sundial/Assets/Art/Textures/dial_paper.png (44892 bytes). Requantising to 8 bits is a visible-change by the census, so it needs a render compare and a Unity licence this machine lacks; it is lossy, so the lossless ledger (0011) does not cover it. Neither file is named in 0012 or 0013. The owner decides per file: requantise at the first Unity session, or keep at 16 bits with a reason. Nothing is changed or moved.

ideas.title: Tests: constructor-guard tests discard the new object
ideas.text: ArgumentGuardParamNameTests.cs:39 (`new DiskSaveIo(directory)`) and SundialServiceGuardTests.cs:32 (`new SundialService(_clock, directory)`) build an object only to see its constructor throw, so CA1806 flags the unused instance. Assign each to a discard (`_ = new ...`). Test code only, no behaviour change, and the 335 tests stay 335. Both files are the guard tests that I1 and I2 added.

ideas.title: Core: KeptDays and KeptDaysFrom share one guard-and-loop
ideas.text: Ledger.cs:147-154 against :180-187 (jscpd, 8 lines, 113 tokens): KeptDays and KeptDaysFrom have the same guard and the same distinct-day loop, and differ by one condition (`e.Day >= firstDay`). Not in the base run; the guard text is the only line I1 (a576eb7) changed in these two blocks, and it added `nameof(habitId)` to each, which plausibly lifted the stretch over the 70-token minimum (not run at a576eb7). A private helper that takes the first day (int.MinValue for none) removes it; no signature changes, so it qualifies under 0012 (c) with the existing Ledger tests.
